limits: Catalog metadata and routing are not evidence of supported answers.
Evidence-path status is distinct from independent answer correctness.
Topics outside the fixed100 corpus are inventoried without claiming they have been evaluated.
New rules extend or overlap existing families; eighteen metadata entries are not eighteen newly correct answer families.
CPF typed payroll calculator is not connected to natural-language fact extraction.
No merge, deployment, source activation, live-model acceptance, or historical ACRA release acceptance.

newRules.title: Commencement of key Corporate and Accounting Laws changes on 20 October 2026
newRules.population: Companies filing annual returns; guarantee companies also have a member-count confirmation
provisions: Corporate and Accounting Laws (Amendment) Act 2025 commencement notice; the notice does not enumerate the amending Act sections.
newRules.rule: From 20 October 2026, an annual-return filer must confirm that current particulars already provided to ACRA are accurate for directors, chief executive officers (CEOs), secretaries, auditors and relevant members. These particulars include names, identification details, nationality, contact address, appointment dates, registered office address and shareholding details where applicable. The form separately asks whether any individual performs the CEO role. A company limited by guarantee must confirm its latest-reported total member count.
conditions: Applies to annual returns filed from the expressly stated commencement date.
Check ACRA-recorded particulars and update inaccurate particulars in Bizfile before filing.
The CEO question concerns individuals performing the role; the ACRA notice does not limit it to a title or appointed position.
exceptions: Companies limited by guarantee have an additional total-number-of-members confirmation.
The notice does not say the CEO question or officer-particulars confirmation changes the underlying duty to appoint or register officers.
requiredFacts: For a particular filing: filing date, company type, existing ACRA particulars, whether individuals perform the CEO role, and whether the company is limited by guarantee.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The official ACRA notice states the commencement date as 20 October 2026. This explicit date supports the transition; it is not inferred from the notice publication or retrieval date.
limitations: General change explanation only; does not verify what particulars are currently recorded for an entity.
Do not apply this change to filings submitted before 20 October 2026 without contemporaneous evidence.
The notice gives examples of particulars and says “where applicable”; it is not a field-by-field eform schema.

newRules.title: Steps to file an annual return
newRules.population: Singapore local companies and their authorised company-officer or CSP filers
provisions: ACRA Bizfile annual-return filing process guidance. The page describes the process and does not replace statutory filing-deadline rules.
newRules.rule: A company officer such as a director or secretary may file a company annual return, or a corporate service provider may file for it. The filer logs in to Bizfile as a Business User through Corppass, checks the company type, registered office address, business activities, company officers, shareholder/share-capital particulars, charges and statutory-register requirements, updates inaccurate entity details before continuing, checks financial-statement duties, and completes company-type declarations and AGM/financial-statement/register sections. The eform asks whether an individual performs the CEO role; a yes answer requires that CEO to be appointed and reflected as a Position Holder. AGM details must be entered even where the company was exempt or dispensed with the AGM. One director signs the directors’ statement for a single-director company; at least two directors sign where there is more than one. The filer reviews, declares and pays the stated S$60 fee. The page also says all overdue annual returns must be filed first when more than one financial year is overdue.
conditions: Filing is through Bizfile’s File annual returns eService; the company data and applicable form sections depend on company type and reporting-period status.
If full XBRL financial statements are filed, a PDF copy is not required; otherwise a complete PDF copy is required for the cases stated on the page.
AGM details are declared whether the company held an AGM, was exempt or dispensed with one.
exceptions: Financial-statement filing exemptions and exceptions depend on the separate ACRA financial-statement rules.
This process page does not establish the statutory annual-return deadline or a historical filing process.
requiredFacts: Entity type and financial-year end.
Company type and status for the financial period.
Current officer, shareholder, share, office, activity and charge information.
Financial-statement filing status, AGM status, director count, and RORC/ROND/RONS obligations.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The process page is marked last updated 19 October 2026. That page-update date is not a legal effective date and is not used to establish the process for an earlier filing.
limitations: This is a general process summary, not confirmation of a particular entity’s statutory filing obligation, deadline, eligibility or completed filing.
The current step sequence and stated S$60 transaction fee may change; year-specific filing process is not established by the page.

newRules.title: Financial statements: Filing requirements and exemptions
newRules.population: Singapore-incorporated companies required to file financial statements; template varies by company type, size and regulatory status
provisions: Companies Act section 201A for dormant relevant company exemption; other categories are described in ACRA guidance without section numbers in the cited passage.
newRules.rule: The ACRA guidance lists simplified XBRL plus an authorised PDF for smaller and non-publicly accountable companies; XBRL FSH (Banks) or XBRL FSH (Insurance) plus an authorised PDF for the regulated bank, finance and insurance group; PDF only for companies limited by guarantee or companies approved to use other standards; and Full XBRL for all other Singapore-incorporated companies required to file financial statements. “Smaller” requires both current-year revenue and assets not exceeding S$500,000. “Non-publicly accountable” also excludes listed and specified regulated entity types. The dormant-relevant-company and solvent-EPC financial-statement exceptions have separate qualification conditions. ACRA labels technical resources as applying from 19 October 2026 onwards and identifies ACRA Taxonomy 2026 resources.
conditions: A company must first determine whether it is required to file financial statements; dormant relevant companies and solvent EPCs may qualify for separate financial-statement exceptions.
Small-company revenue and asset thresholds must both be met; group consolidation and currency translation details apply under the ACRA definitions page.
The Full/Simplified/FSH/PDF template depends on the company’s exact status and regulatory category.
exceptions: Dormant relevant companies need not prepare/file only if all Companies Act section 201A requirements are met, including the assets, dormancy and listing/subsidiary conditions.
A solvent EPC meeting an EPC definition may elect not to file financial statements but may file voluntarily; its annual-return solvency declaration still applies.
Foreign companies with Singapore branches and some individually approved cases are addressed elsewhere on the ACRA filing guidance and are not classified by this local-company rule summary.
requiredFacts: Local/foreign incorporation, company form and whether it is a company limited by guarantee.
Required-to-file/exempt status, dormancy history, listed/subsidiary status and group assets.
Current-year revenue and assets, consolidation and currency facts.
Public-accountability or MAS regulatory status.
EPC status and solvency, where relevant.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The ACRA page explicitly labels “XBRL filing requirements (from 19 October 2026 onwards)” and points to ACRA Taxonomy 2026. The page itself is marked last updated 20 October 2026. Only the labeled XBRL boundary is used for transition-date claims; publication/retrieval dates do not establish another rule’s effective date.
limitations: Does not determine an individual company’s template without classification facts.
The complete definitions and section 201A eligibility must be checked against ACRA’s linked guidance and law.
Do not apply the current page or 19 October 2026 XBRL boundary to a historical filing unless the relevant year-specific official source supports it.

newRules.title: Annual leave eligibility and entitlement
newRules.population: Employees covered by the Employment Act who have served the employer at least three months
provisions: Employment Act annual-leave guidance; the registry associates this statutory subject with section 88A, but the cited page excerpt does not itself give a section reference.
newRules.rule: An Employment Act-covered employee becomes entitled to paid annual leave after at least 3 months; being on probation does not remove that entitlement. For 3 to 12 months of service, the entitlement is based on completed months worked even if the employee is still on probation. The minimum annual entitlement rises by one day per year from 7 days in year one to 14 days from year eight. The official formula is completed months of service divided by 12, multiplied by the annual leave entitlement; fractions less than one-half of a day round down, while half or more rounds up to one day. Approved unpaid leave is excluded; service during a resignation notice period counts.
conditions: The Employment Act must cover the employee and at least three months’ service must be completed; probation does not remove entitlement after this threshold.
For 3 to 12 months of service, pro-rating uses completed months even if the employee is still on probation; a partial, incomplete service month is disregarded.
The minimum table follows year of service beginning on the employment start date.
exceptions: For employees outside the Employment Act, use contractual terms; this page does not establish their statutory entitlement.
Annual leave on half-working days, unused-leave carry-forward/forfeiture and termination encashment have separate rules.
requiredFacts: Employment Act coverage and start date.
Completed service months and service year.
Annual contractual entitlement, approved unpaid-leave periods, and notice period if pro-rating.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: Current MOM guidance does not state an effective date for the displayed table. Historical entitlement for a named past year is unresolved from this page alone.
limitations: States the general statutory minimum and pro-rating method; it does not calculate an individual balance without the listed facts.
The current page’s retrieval or update date is not treated as legal commencement.

newRules.title: Sick leave eligibility and entitlement
newRules.population: Employees covered by the Employment Act after at least three months with the employer
provisions: Employment Act sick-leave guidance; the registry associates this statutory subject with section 89, but the cited page excerpt does not itself give a section reference.
newRules.rule: An Employment Act-covered employee with at least 3 months’ service who informs, or tries to inform, the employer within 48 hours may qualify for paid outpatient sick and hospitalisation leave on the applicable medical certification. The example entitlement is 5 days of outpatient sick leave and 15 days of hospitalisation leave at month 3; 8 outpatient and 30 hospitalisation days at month 4; 11 outpatient and 45 hospitalisation days at month 5; and from month 6, 14 days of outpatient leave and 60 days of hospitalisation leave. The 60-day hospitalisation cap includes outpatient leave.
conditions: The Employment Act applies, at least 3 months of service are completed, and the employer is notified or attempted to be notified within 48 hours.
Outpatient leave requires a registered medical or dental practitioner’s certification.
Hospitalisation leave must meet the specified care/quarantine conditions and certification requirements.
exceptions: The 60 hospitalisation days include the 14 outpatient days; they are not 60 days in addition to outpatient leave.
Historical table application is not established by this current page.
Cosmetic procedures are not required paid sick leave under the page.
requiredFacts: Employment Act coverage, employment start date and service months completed.
When the employer was informed, qualifying medical certificate and whether care satisfies the hospitalisation definition.
Outpatient and hospitalisation leave already taken in the relevant entitlement year.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: Current MOM guidance does not state an effective date for the displayed table. Historical entitlement is unresolved from this page alone.
limitations: General entitlement only; case eligibility and remaining balance require the listed employee, notice, certification and leave-use facts.
Do not infer the applicable historical table from page retrieval date.

newRules.title: Public holidays: entitlement and pay
newRules.population: Employees covered by the Employment Act; contractual terms govern employees outside its coverage
provisions: Employment Act public-holiday guidance. No Act section number is supplied by this source excerpt.
newRules.rule: An Employment Act-covered employee has 11 paid public holidays each year. If a holiday falls on the rest day, the following working day will be a paid public holiday; if it falls on a non-working day, another day off or an extra day at the gross rate is due. Working on a public holiday ordinarily earns holiday gross pay plus an additional day at the basic rate; overtime applies beyond normal hours. By mutual agreement, the day may be substituted. Part IV coverage limits which employees may use time off in lieu.
conditions: Distinguish a holiday on a working day, non-working day, or rest day.

For holiday gross pay, the employee must not be absent without consent or reasonable excuse on the working day immediately before or after the holiday; authorised leave on either day is permitted. No holiday pay is due when the holiday itself falls during approved unpaid leave.
Additional basic-rate pay is the default for working on the holiday; substitute-holiday arrangements require mutual agreement.
exceptions: An employee outside Employment Act coverage is governed by the contract.
Time off in lieu of hours worked is available only to employees not covered by Part IV under the stated arrangement.
Rest-day pay and any excess-hours overtime are separate entitlements.
requiredFacts: Employment Act and Part IV coverage.
Work schedule and whether the date is a working, non-working or rest day.
Whether the employee worked, hours worked, agreed substitution/time-off arrangements, and relevant absence or unpaid-leave facts.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: Current MOM guidance gives no explicit effective-date boundary for the general entitlement. Historical application is unresolved from this source alone.
limitations: Does not decide a specific date’s gazetted holiday status or compute holiday pay without schedule and wage facts.
Does not replace separate rest-day, overtime or part-time rules.

newRules.title: Paying salary: final salary deadlines
newRules.population: Employees covered by the Employment Act and their employers
provisions: Employment Act salary-payment guidance; cited page does not specify relevant section numbers for the four termination deadlines.
newRules.rule: MOM distinguishes final wages by how employment ends: where an employee serves required resignation notice, pay on the last day of employment; resignation without notice, within 7 days of the last day of employment; misconduct dismissal, on the last day of employment or within 3 working days from dismissal if that is not possible; and employer termination, on the last day of employment or within 3 working days from termination if that is not possible.
conditions: The rule is for employees covered by the Employment Act.
Determine which of the four termination paths applies; resignation with notice and without notice have different deadlines.
exceptions: Foreign employees leaving employment have a separate tax clearance withholding requirement, which may withhold salary and leave pay for up to 30 days after the cessation notice to the Comptroller.
Commission-payment timing may depend on contract, policies or practices.
The current page does not establish historical applicability.
requiredFacts: Employment Act coverage and whether employee resigned with notice, resigned without notice, was dismissed for misconduct, or was terminated by the employer.
Last employment day or termination/dismissal date.
Any foreign-employee tax-clearance notice and contract-specific commission terms.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The current MOM page states these payment timelines but gives no effective date for them. Past termination cases need contemporaneous statutory evidence.
limitations: General rule summary; does not decide a dispute about notice validity, breach, misconduct, wrongful dismissal or amounts owed.
Tax-clearance withholding is a separate issue and depends on the foreign employee and cessation-notice facts.

newRules.title: Conditions for Claiming Input Tax
authorityAndProvisions: GST (General) Regulations regulation 26, as identified in IRAS guidance
newRules.population: GST-registered businesses claiming GST on staff medical expenses
newRules.rule: Staff medical input tax is generally blocked by regulation 26. Subject to ordinary input-tax conditions, IRAS lists expenses obligatory under WICA or a qualifying IRA collective agreement. For medical treatment connected to a work-related health risk or requirement for expenses incurred on or after 1 October 2021, the detailed conditions require either Singapore written law concerning the treatment/facility/practitioner or COVID-19 treatment required by a government/public-authority written advisory.
conditions: The claim must still meet the general conditions for input tax.
For the post-1 October 2021 work-risk route, the applicable written-law or COVID-19 advisory limb must also be met.
exceptions: An ordinary staff health benefit does not by itself meet the described criteria.
IRAS specifically says Primary Care Plan expenses do not qualify on the described facts.
requiredFacts: Expense and treatment date.
Whether WICA or an applicable collective agreement makes the expense obligatory.
If relying on the later exception, the work-related health risk/requirement and whether the claim relies on written law or COVID-19 advisory treatment.
GST registration, business use and supporting invoice/claim facts.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: IRAS expressly says the work-related health-risk exception applies to medical treatment for expenses incurred on or after 1 October 2021. This does not establish a historical rule for other periods.
limitations: The retained fixture is the complete native IRAS page response captured on 26 October 2026; the capture date does not establish legal applicability.
This states the regulation 26 general rule and listed exception criteria, not a case conclusion or complete input-tax eligibility determination.
The linked table summary says “written law or advisory”; the page’s detailed condition limits its advisory limb to COVID-19 treatment. Do not omit that qualification.
Do not extend the post-2021 exception to unrelated medical, insurance or private expenses.

newRules.title: Conditions for Claiming Input Tax — Motor Vehicles
authorityAndProvisions: GST (General) Regulations regulations 25(1) and 27, as identified in IRAS guidance
newRules.population: GST-registered businesses incurring motor-car and motor-vehicle expenses
newRules.rule: Purchase and running input tax on a motor car is generally disallowed under regulation 27 unless the vehicle is excluded from the regulation 25(1) definition or a stated situation falls outside regulation 27. IRAS describes eligible pay-per-trip chauffeured private-hire transport from 1 April 2022, third-party use expenses from 1 January 2023, and other vehicles such as lorries, vans and motorcycles that are not motor cars, in each case subject to ordinary input-tax conditions.
conditions: A stated exception remains subject to the ordinary conditions for claiming input tax.
Connected-person use additionally requires expense recovery and a recovery that is not ancillary to a primary supply; a partial recovery limits the claim to the recovered part.
exceptions: Cars physically or economically used by the claimant or its employees remain disallowed.
Connected-person car expenses remain disallowed unless both express recovery conditions are met.
A private-hire transport exception concerns a chauffeured point-A-to-point-B pay-per-trip service and valid invoice evidence, not purchase or lease of a car.
requiredFacts: Whether the expense is car acquisition/running expense or transport service.
Vehicle category and who used the car, including physical and economic use.
For private-hire transport, pay-per-trip service and valid tax invoice.
For third-party/connected-person use, user relationship, recovery amount, and whether recovery is ancillary.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: IRAS expressly dates the private-hire service exception from 1 April 2022 and the cited third-party/connected-person rules from 1 January 2023. These displayed dates do not establish unrelated historical motor-car rules.
limitations: The retained fixture is the complete native IRAS page response captured on 26 October 2026; the capture date does not establish legal applicability.
Does not classify a particular vehicle against the statutory definition or establish the complete rules for every motor-vehicle arrangement.
Do not infer transaction-period treatment from the page retrieval date.

newRules.title: Estimated Chargeable Income (ECI) Filing
authorityAndProvisions: IRAS ECI filing guidance; the displayed excerpt identifies Income Tax Act 1947 section 43(2) for one named REIT category and sections 35(14), 35(12), and 35(12A) for the stated unit-trust note
newRules.population: Singapore companies determining ECI filing obligations for a Year of Assessment
newRules.rule: A company generally files ECI within 3 months after financial year-end unless it meets the filing waiver or is specifically not required to file. The general waiver requires BOTH annual revenue of S$5 million or less for the financial year and nil ECI for the YA, measured before partial/start-up tax exemption. Revenue means the company’s main source of income; for an investment holding company it is investment income. Nil ECI alone, a book loss alone, or revenue alone does not establish the waiver.
conditions: Both waiver tests must be met for the relevant YA.
If the company is in a listed category specifically not required to file, that is a separate route from the general waiver.
A qualifying waiver is self-assessed; the source says no IRAS confirmation or notice is needed.
exceptions: A company with nil ECI but annual revenue above S$5 million must still file.
Revenue at or below S$5 million with positive ECI must still file.

The displayed category list includes foreign ship owners/charterers with a shipping return, foreign universities, designated/approved CPF unit trusts, qualifying section 43(2) REITs, and cases specifically waived by IRAS.
requiredFacts: Applicable financial year-end and YA.
Revenue from the principal/main income source (investment income for an investment holding company).
Tax ECI before partial/start-up exemption, not accounting profit or post-exemption taxable amount.
Whether a specifically excluded/waived entity category applies.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The official page provides current general wording and a worked example explicitly labelled for FYE 30 June 2024; that example is not taken as a complete historical effective-date statement for the current threshold.
limitations: The $5 million threshold and current examples are not projected to a historical or future YA without period-specific evidence.
ECI is taxable profits after tax-allowable expenses, not a direct synonym for accounting profit.
Does not calculate ECI or conclude the company-specific waiver without YA, revenue and tax-computation facts.
The retained fixture is the complete native IRAS page response captured on 26 October 2026; the capture date is not used as a legal applicability date.

newRules.title: Payments that are subject to withholding tax
authorityAndProvisions: Income Tax Act 1947 section 12(7)(b) and (c), as described in the linked IRAS service-payment guidance; treaty relief depends on the relevant DTA
newRules.population: Singapore payers paying specified service/management income to a non-resident company
newRules.rule: For covered technical or management services paid to a non-resident company, WHT applies to fees attributable to work done in Singapore. Work performed partly overseas is apportioned to its Singapore-work portion. IRAS states a current 17% prevailing Corporate Income Tax rate on gross Singapore service fees, subject to the applicable DTA and facts; overseas electronic services without staff sent to Singapore are described as performed outside Singapore.
conditions: Identify whether the payee is a non-resident company and whether the payment is technical/management service income in scope.
Determine where work was physically performed and allocate mixed-location fees.
Review the payee’s residence, any Singapore permanent establishment, and the relevant DTA before applying a rate.
exceptions: Services provided electronically from overseas without sending staff are stated to be performed outside Singapore.
Relevant DTAs can change treatment/rates, including permanent-establishment and technical-services provisions.
The old cost-pooling administrative concession applied only to payments liable before 1 November 2022; IRAS says it was withdrawn for payments liable on/after that date.
requiredFacts: Payee legal/person type and tax residence.
Nature of service and contractual scope.
Singapore versus overseas work and basis for apportionment.
Service provision year, payment due/credit/actual dates, DTA and permanent-establishment facts.
Whether payer bears tax and must gross up the contractual payment.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The cited page states the cost-pooling concession boundary of 1 November 2022. The 17% rate is shown as the prevailing rate, without a complete historical rate table in this excerpt; it is not applied to historical/future service years by retrieval date.
limitations: The cited page’s service-rate example is for non-resident companies; non-resident individuals/professionals have separate rules.
The 17% prevailing rate is not universal: DTA provisions and relevant facts may change treatment.
The retained page does not provide a complete treaty-specific rate table or the full statutory analysis for every payment type.

newRules.title: Withholding Tax (WHT) filing and payment due date
authorityAndProvisions: IRAS WHT filing and payment guidance
newRules.population: Singapore payers required to file WHT on payments to non-residents
newRules.rule: File and pay WHT by the 15th of the second month from the IRAS-defined date of payment. For most payments that date is the earliest of contractual due date (or invoice date if no agreement, ignoring credit terms), credit to an account designated by the non-resident, and actual payment. Director fees have a separate entitlement timing rule.
conditions: Use the statutory/IRAS defined payment date rather than automatically using cash remittance date.
For director fees, distinguish arrears approval from advance approval before finding the earliest entitlement date.
exceptions: WHT must still be filed when an applicable DTA or ARI reduces the rate to zero.
GIRO deduction is normally the 25th of the month the tax is due, moved to the next working day for a weekend/public holiday.
Eligible multiple payments for the same engagement to a non-resident professional/public entertainer within 60 days may be consolidated under the stated conditions.
requiredFacts: Payment type and any director-fee status.
Contract payment-due date, invoice date, credit date and actual payment date.
Payee/person and whether a special consolidation or exemption applies.
Applicable tax due month and public holidays for GIRO.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: IRAS page says last updated 14 August 2026 but the excerpt does not state a complete historical effective period; it is treated as current general guidance only.
limitations: Does not calculate an actual calendar due date without payment facts and calendar context.
The page does not enumerate every special payment rule or replace payment-specific guidance.
An exemption from WHT amount does not by itself remove the stated filing requirement.

newRules.title: Notice SFA 04-N24 — Reporting of Misconduct of Representatives
authorityAndProvisions: Securities and Futures Act 2001 sections 99(1)(a)–(d) and 101(1); Notice SFA 04-N24 paragraphs 1, 2, 5, 20 and 21
newRules.population: Holders of a capital markets services licence and persons exempt under SFA section 99(1)(a), (b), (c) or (d), regarding their current/former representatives
newRules.rule: Notice SFA 04-N24 takes effect on 1 January 2027. It applies to CMS licence holders and persons exempt under SFA section 99(1)(a)–(d), for misconduct by their current or former representatives. A CMI must submit a Misconduct Report no later than 21 calendar days after first having reasonable grounds to believe the representative committed misconduct, or such longer period as MAS allows in writing. Paragraphs 20–21 set transition rules for matters with pre-2027 reasonable grounds or reports already filed/due under the cancelled notice.
conditions: The subject is a current representative, or a former representative concerning misconduct during the representative period.
The 21-calendar-day period starts when the CMI first has reasonable grounds to believe the representative committed misconduct.
A longer reporting period applies only if the Authority allows it in writing.
exceptions: For defined unfiled pre-2027 matters, paragraph 20 requires a report within 21 calendar days after 1 January 2027, or a longer period allowed in writing.
Paragraph 21 keeps the cancelled Notice applicable where a report was submitted before 1 January 2027 or was required by 31 December 2026.
requiredFacts: Whether the entity is a CMS licence holder or exempt under SFA section 99(1)(a)–(d).
Whether the subject was a representative when the alleged conduct occurred.
The date first reasonable grounds arose.
Whether a report was submitted under the cancelled Notice before 1 January 2027 or was due by 31 December 2026.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The Notice itself says it takes effect on 1 January 2027, cancels SFA 04-N11 that day, and states transitional provisions for pre-2027 matters. The notice issue date (30 December 2025) is not treated as its effective date.
limitations: This bounded rule covers the Notice commencement, covered CMI population, initial Misconduct Report deadline and transitional provisions only; it does not explain Investigation Reports, Update Reports or all misconduct categories.
It is manager-level reporting about representatives and does not establish fund/VCC-level return requirements or QDC reporting.
The retained visible-text excerpt is limited to paragraphs 1, 2, 5, 20 and 21; the native official PDF is the primary document.
A company-specific conclusion requires the CMI status, representative period, reasonable-grounds date and transition facts.

newRules.title: CPF Contribution Rate Table from 1 January 2026
newRules.population: Employees of private-sector employers and non-pensionable employees of ministries, statutory bodies and aided schools who are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents
newRules.rule: The official 2026 table has five schedules: full rates for Singapore Citizens and third-year-onward SPRs; graduated employer/graduated employee rates for first- and second-year SPRs; and, after CPF Board approval, full employer/graduated employee schedules for first- and second-year SPRs. Each schedule varies by the table’s age bands and monthly total-wage bands, with Ordinary Wages capped at S$8,000 and Additional Wages capped separately.
provisions: CPF Act 1953 First Schedule contribution rates, as presented in CPF Board’s Tables 1–5; this module does not independently interpret the Schedule text.
conditions: The retained table states rates from 1 January 2026.
Use the first-year or second-year PR schedule only within the corresponding PR-status year.
Full employer/graduated employee or full employer/full employee options for first/second year require a joint higher-rate application and CPF Board approval.
The PDF expressly scopes its tables to private-sector and non-pensionable employees.
exceptions: Pensionable public-service employees, platform workers, self-employed persons, wages not classified as CPF-payable OW/AW, and rates outside the 2026 table are not calculated by this module.
The 2027 update notice means 2026 rates must not be reused for 2027 payroll.
requiredFacts: Contribution month in 2026.
Singapore Citizen or SPR status; for an SPR, conversion date and applicable table/election.
Date of birth, since an age-group rate changes from the first day of the month after a 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Private-sector or non-pensionable employment scope.
The classified OW and AW amounts payable for the month.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The document titles all five tables “from 1 January 2026”. CPF Board’s computation page, retained separately, states that senior-employee rates increase from 1 January 2027. The source does not establish a single end date for every age group.
limitations: Only the 2026 tables are retained. Do not apply them to 2025 or 2027.
The retained text excerpt is extracted from the retained original official PDF bytes; its digest is recorded separately from the PDF digest.

newRules.title: How much CPF contributions to pay
newRules.population: CPF-contributing employers and employees; private-sector / non-pensionable table computations
newRules.rule: Choose a contribution table from citizenship or SPR year, then age group and monthly wage band; compute on Total Wages made up of Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages, subject to their separate ceilings. Where monthly total wages are above S$50 and at or below S$500, the employee share is nil while the employer share is payable. Round the combined total contribution to the nearest dollar (50 cents rounds up), discard cents from the employee share, and calculate employer share as total less employee share.
provisions: CPF Board’s published employer computation sequence; the public page identifies the Central Provident Fund Act contribution framework but does not set out a paragraph number in the retained passage.
conditions: The 2026 summary rate table applies to Singaporeans and SPRs from year three onward with monthly wages above S$750.
Select the correct full or graduated SPR table and age group before calculating.
When OW and AW are both payable, calculate and sum the contributions for both before applying the rounding rules.
exceptions: An employee earning exactly S$50 or less is below the page’s contribution threshold.
The retained high-level page does not reproduce the full graduated rate schedules; consult the linked 2026 PDF for those rates.
requiredFacts: Contribution period, status/PR year, birthday, wage components, applicable ceilings and whether an SPR higher-rate election was approved.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The page identifies the summary as rates from 1 January 2026 and separately reports that senior-worker contribution rates increase from 1 January 2027.
limitations: A general method explanation does not determine a company’s actual payroll without employee and wage facts.
This retained excerpt does not support historical rates or the detailed contribution amount for cases outside the linked 2026 tables.

newRules.title: What is the Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling?
newRules.population: Employees subject to CPF contributions on Ordinary Wages
newRules.rule: The monthly Ordinary Wage ceiling is S$8,000 from 1 January 2026; the official table also gives prior dated ceilings and keeps the annual salary ceiling at S$102,000 through the listed periods.
conditions: Apply the dated value for the payroll period rather than using the current amount for another year.
The S$8,000 ceiling is monthly and applies to OW, not to the independent AW ceiling.
exceptions: The retained page does not provide all possible exception or special-population rules for every public-service employment regime.
requiredFacts: The payroll year or date, employee/employment coverage and the amount classified as OW.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The official table specifies S$7,400 for 1 January–31 December 2025 and S$8,000 from 1 January 2026.
limitations: It gives the ceiling, not the amount or rate of an individual contribution.
The page was last updated 14 August 2026; that retrieval/update date is not used as a legal effective date.

newRules.title: Examples for computation of Additional Wage (AW) Ceiling
newRules.population: Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents, for each employer and calendar year
newRules.rule: The annual AW ceiling equals S$102,000 minus Ordinary Wages subject to CPF for the year. At an AW payment, estimate the ceiling using the year’s expected OW, subtract AW already subject to CPF, and cap the current AW at the available remainder. Recalculate using actual OW in the last month of employment or December, whichever occurs first; adjust any shortfall and seek a refund for excess contributions.
provisions: CPF Board AW-ceiling computation examples and employer instructions.
conditions: The ceiling is per employer, per year, and applies to Singapore Citizens and SPRs.
Use the year in which the AW is due and payable: a 2025 bonus payable in 2026 uses 2026 limits.
At non-final AW payments, use a supported estimate of OW expected for the whole year; at final settlement, use actual OW up through that payroll month.
exceptions: First-/second-year SPRs use their applicable contribution-rate tables even though the AW ceiling formula is the same.
A refund or shortfall on prior payments requires review of the payroll already submitted; this calculator only determines current eligible AW and does not submit adjustments.
requiredFacts: Due-and-payable year and date.
Current AW amount and prior AW already subject to CPF for this employer/year.
Actual prior OW subject to CPF and either the complete expected annual OW subject to CPF or an identified final month of employment/year.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The official examples state that the AW payable-date year controls and expressly show the 2026 ceiling calculation using S$102,000 and the S$8,000 monthly OW ceiling.
limitations: The retained text excerpt is extracted from the retained original official PDF bytes; its digest is recorded separately from the PDF digest.
A future OW estimate is a required input before final settlement and can change; a source retrieval date cannot supply it.

newRules.title: I have successfully applied for a new re-entry permit and retained my Singapore Permanent Resident status. How will this impact my CPF contributions?
newRules.population: Singapore Permanent Residents earning wages in Singapore
newRules.rule: First-year rates apply from the date PR status is obtained to the last day of the month of the first anniversary. Second-year rates apply from the following month through the last day of the month of the second anniversary. Third-year rates start in the month after that second anniversary.
provisions: CPF Board’s PR-year instructions, referring to the ICA Entry Permit Form 5/5A as the status-date evidence.
conditions: Use the Entry Permit date as the date status was obtained.
The year transitions occur by calendar month; the second and third years begin on the first day of the month following the relevant anniversary.
exceptions: The first calendar month may begin partway through the month on the actual PR-conversion date.
A jointly elected higher contribution basis during the first two years requires CPF Board approval; year calculation by itself does not prove an election.
requiredFacts: Date PR status was obtained.
Contribution month.
Whether a higher contribution option was jointly requested and approved, if applicable.
newRules.effectiveDateEvidence: The rule is described on a CPF Board page last updated 11 March 2026; the page does not identify a separate commencement date for the displayed PR-year method.
limitations: This rule selects the PR year only; rates still require the official table for the payroll year and a supported election.
The example date is illustrative and does not establish retroactive rates for any other historical period.
